How bridges, stablecoin issuers and pools can form one pDAI
support system
1 October 2026. Read-only research. This study extends the white paper (main paper). Protocol names
below identify candidate contract families; they do not identify the people controlling their keys.
The integrated mechanism
The strongest version of the proposal combines three sources of usable inventory: bridges that return
existing local tokens; issuers that create existing local tokens against accepted collateral or authorized
credit; and locally earned proceeds. A shared operator could move that inventory among Curve, Aave,
Balancer and ordinary liquidity pools. Supply controllers could replenish an expensive stablecoin or retire
an excess one. The operator would buy cheap eligible units, sell expensive units and preserve both sides
of its conversion promise.
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 240

Every arrow is a separate asset conversion or contract permission. L1 here means PulseChain; L2 means
the proposed pARB environment. Its present source deployments were not accessible in this research.
Ethereum and ordinary Arbitrum documentation establish upstream designs, not a running pARB
deployment.
The important improvement is that local reissuance is optional when a bridge already returns
the token the destination pool accepts. New collateral adapters matter when the output is a
different representation or when existing escrow cannot provide enough inventory.
The subsequent dedicated sUSD study (Appendix 66) adds its six inherited pool connections, mUSD
basket acceptance and copied Synthetix issuer-specific synth bridge. It illustrates why the final pool-
facing L1 address matters even when source addresses differ, and why issuer minting must be
distinguished from pARB escrow release. Its fresh destination observations retain their separate block
27,683,120 identity.

still separate contracts and supplies. Second, a bridge can return the exact existing L1 address, even
though the L2 address differs. Both can fit existing L1 infrastructure; the second is sufficient for an
existing Curve coin.

this counterpart. The registered USDC is the older bridged USDC identity, not every Arbitrum token
called USDC.
Literal identical numeric addresses were found for three configured pairs: Plenny PL2
(0x3642c0680329ae3e103e2b5ab29ddfed4d43cbe5), Hashgold HGOLD (0x445164d9e038e1dae0989e4b6ac745b78d26f181) and
MCDEX/MUX MCB (0x4e352cf164e64adcbad318c3a1e222e9eba4ce42). Historical L1 metadata supplies their names.

The checkpoint gateway token balance was zero for DAI, USDT, OUSD, Reserve eUSD, mUSD and FRAX;
USDC had 1,000,000 raw units, ordinarily one USDC at six decimals. These are balances at the
selected gateway, not total ecosystem resources or all Across liquidity. An authenticated withdrawal
cannot obtain an unlimited amount from an empty escrow. HGOLD's token permissions remain
incompletely verified. PL2/MCB use the custom escrow gateway; their same-address configuration does
not change its release model.
There are real token-specific mint branches. The saved bridge inventory (Appendix 4) verifies postfork
ARB reverse-gateway minting and GRT shortfall minting under a token-specific allowance. LPT has a
mint-on-shortfall design whose complete current issuer permissions remain unresolved. Those findings
support specialized mint routes; they do not grant the same powers over DAI, USDC or every receipt.
The 136-token bridge identity table retains mapping, calculated counterpart, registration result and raw
gateway balance. The source chain was not queried, so these are configured destination identities rather
than a list of proven live pARB assets.
Which tokens actually provide supply buffers?
“Supply buffer” has three useful forms. A rebase changes eligible holders' balances. Authorized
venue supply management mints tokens into a pool or withdraws and burns them. Collateral
issuance/redemption creates and retires tokens against an accepted asset or debt position. All can
change available inventory, but they require different actions and obligations.

Frax documents the historical Curve AMO. Inverse documents Fed expansion and contraction. These
primary descriptions support the supply-controller mechanism; they do not demonstrate the current
copied contracts' execution rights or live capacity. Later upstream versions must not be imported into
the inherited design without matching deployed code.
The OUSD pool 0x87650d7bbfc3a9f10587d7778206671719d9910d returns rebaseState=0 and a nonzero 
nonRebasingCreditsPerToken. The inherited OUSD source uses a separate fixed credits-per-token value for
nonrebasing accounts. Contract accounts default to that behavior unless eligible opt-in applies. This
agrees with Origin's rebase documentation. Pool membership alone therefore does not establish a yield-
rebase buffer.
The verified UZD source at 0xb40b6608b2743e691c9b54ddbdee7bf03cd79f1c implements separate elastic and rigid

issuance is not established. The exact verified source response and saved getter responses are retained.
Gro describes PWRD's rebasing tranche, Lybra describes its own eUSD balance model, and Matrixdock
documents STBT's rebase and transfer restrictions. These architectures are candidate mechanisms, not
current PulseChain yield results. Gro's upstream wind-down notice also prevents assuming its original
yield operation continues unchanged.
A token rebase does not ensure an old pool recognizes increased balances as tradable LP inventory.
Inspect the exact pool's stored balances, rate adapters and accounting. Curve's older registry source
distinguishes pool balances from excess token balances treated as admin balances. Newer StableSwap
NG explicitly handles rebasing assets, but that later implementation is not automatically installed in the
May 2023 pools. Changing an excluded account to rebasing without compatible pool accounting could
misallocate yield or break assumptions; it is not a demonstrated peg action.
Modern Mountain Protocol USDM must not be confused with the inherited Mochi USDM at 
0x31d4eb09a216e181ec8a43ce79226a487d6f0ba9; Mochi identifies it in its deployment list. The final canonical
crvUSD address 0xf939e0a03fb07f59a73314e73794be0e57ac1b4e returns no code at the inherited boundary. Three

crvUSD/PegKeeper or GHO designs cannot be silently assumed to operate in that inherited catalogue.
What governance control is actually confirmed?
There are three different questions: which contract has authority; who has enough votes or signer access
to make it act; and whether the proposed group controls those people or keys. A token's owner() getter
usually answers only part of the first question. Acquiring governance tokens can change voting control
while every owner address stays unchanged.

Across transaction evidence is in the control study (Appendix 3): Hub ownership transfer and module
ownership transfer. These establish two authority changes within Across, not two independent protocol
acquisitions. They do not establish common human ownership, ownership of UMA itself or the intent to
support pDAI.
Per-family candidate authorities and all returned token addresses are listed below and in authority-
comparisons.csv. A full voting takeover proof would additionally need delegation/checkpoint votes,
proposal thresholds/quorum, voting periods, the executable proposal outcome, timelock eligibility and
any veto/guardian/upgrade powers. Multisigs require threshold signers and enabled modules. Centralized
tokens require their specific mint/upgrade paths. No universal “owns governance” flag represents all
these designs.
Why coordinated control would be valuable
As an inference about the proposed design, coordinated control could install receipt adapters, change
accepted baskets, maintain rate feeds, authorize AMOs/Feds/minters, direct protocol revenues, and
allocate owned liquidity and incentives. That would help connect financing and market operations
without changing every Curve pool's coin list. Existing-token issuance and ordinary swaps often require
issuer authority rather than Curve governance.
Those are reasons a coordinated operator might seek control. They do not prove why an observed
address transfer occurred. The wider common-control hypothesis needs attributable wallet and
executed-governance evidence. It is not required to buy or trade an immutable coin such as LUSD
through an ordinary permitted route.
Add native L1 yield as a second defense
Native assets can contribute reserves and earnings without the L2 round trip. The shortest candidate
route is owned native position → collected proceeds → accepted local stable collateral → issuer
or market → support inventory. It does not require Origin or Reserve to directly accept the original
native token.

Origin's sampled vault accepts DAI/USDC/USDT, not PLS/HEX/PLSX/INC. Harvesting a native position and
converting proceeds into accepted collateral is the easier branch. A new vault strategy, wrapper or
collateral type requires a compatible authority and valuation path. The report does not certify native
“staking in Origin” as an existing public product.
Reserve eUSD's sampled basket consists of four lending receipts; its RSR staking backstop is a separate
function. Adding a native asset or LP claim to that basket requires a compatible collateral plugin,
registration, valuation and activated basket. A separately configured RT oken can be explored. A native-
asset basket may track a volatile index; a $1 accounting label does not remove its collateral's changing
purchasing power. Newer upstream index products cannot be assumed to exist in the copied May 2023
RT oken contracts. See the Reserve collateral audit (Appendix 18).
Keep immediately usable support assets outside long-maturity positions. Native receipts used as
collateral are encumbered; their principal cannot simultaneously fund exits. Multiple PLS/HEX/PLSX/INC
exposures may fall together. Their locally realized value can defend local parity, but an external dollar
promise must use current realizable valuations, haircuts and available conversion. Fees from trading only
among controlled accounts cancel in consolidated accounting; collectible payments from outside
participants are different.
Close the Curve–Aave–Balancer loop
The integrated thesis is an inventory and supply-management network with arbitrage between
its venues. A local stablecoin accepted as one accounting unit can connect markets. A working issuer
conversion can create an actionable trading opportunity; its accounting oracle alone does not make the
opportunity executable.

For example, if an Origin mint accepts one pDAI for one OUSD and a funded market pays 0.99 pUSDC for
that OUSD, buying the pDAI for 0.80 pUSDC can leave 0.19 pUSDC before all fees, costs and risks. The
route creates buying pressure on pDAI and selling pressure on OUSD. Its executable size depends on the
issuer's current valuation/eligibility and the pool's actual bid. Quotes and balances change as trades
execute. The example is conditional arithmetic, not a measured profitable route at the checkpoint.
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 247

If all connected ordinary dollar-unit coins have working conversions and available inventory, similar
trades can narrow differences throughout their connected markets. FRAX/DOLA-style supply operators
could mint/deploy where their own coin is scarce and withdraw/burn where it is excessive. Another issuer
could accept accumulated cheap collateral and supply its existing coin. Ordinary LP deposits and
withdrawals could redistribute liquidity. Yield proceeds could replenish the buffer. The system need not
trade all pools in the same transaction or obtain governance over every coin.
The direction matters. Minting a metacoin and selling it for pDAI supports pDAI but consumes the
metapool's counter-assets and increases its metacoin balance. Repeating that sale without a return path
can destabilize that issuer's market. A complete loop therefore needs a policy for restoring each venue's
useful inventory and meeting issuer redemption/bridge obligations, not just acquiring pDAI once.
Aave is a collateral, debt and available-cash venue; its oracle is not an AMM bid. A funded supply/
withdrawal, valid borrowing/repayment or eligible receipt conversion is the route. Balancer has its own
swaps, rate-provider/wrapper gates, reserve cash and limits. Curve base tokens such as 3CRV/FRAXBP
are LP claims. Their pools can be linked, but they are not interchangeable unlimited one-dollar counters.
Normalize decimals, FX targets and receipt conversion rates before comparing prices. aToken interest,
cToken exchange rates, LP virtual prices, bLUSD appreciation, RAI's redemption target and
FPI's index cannot all be treated as one raw token = $1. Some assets are genuinely foreign
currencies; they can help route liquidity at appropriate exchange rates rather than being forcibly priced
at a dollar.
A crucial boundary remains: relative arbitrage can make several local coins trade near one another even
when the whole group has weak external dollar purchasing power. T o claim actual $1 purchasing power,
name and fund the conversion to an independently priced reference asset. An ETH/BTC pool can provide
an exit when funded; its market rate changes with those assets and does not itself define one dollar.
Relative convergence, inventory coverage and external dollar conversion are three separate
measurements.
What would make this an operating system?
Choose a useful connected subset and give each route an address, authority, available size, full delay
and exit operation. Preserve bridge finality/challenge times, governance delays, basket warm-ups and
replenishing mint limits, native stake maturities, ten-second purchase scheduling and open Portal/debt
obligations. A long financing horizon is compatible with this design; each immediate conversion promise
still needs deliverable inventory while slower resources are pending.
Measure both trade directions after fees; count shared 3pool reserves and nested collateral only once;
specify issuer supply expansion and contraction; and measure the loss of capacity when a bridge, oracle
or issuer fails. The new identity census proves what was registered at the inherited boundary. The
current getters prove specific configurations and exclusions. No state-changing operation or end-to-end
funded mint/bridge/arbitrage campaign was executed.
Reproduction and evidence limits
Inputs, raw requests/responses, failure records, curation and outputs are in artifacts/pulsechain-integrated-
network-20261001/; explicit manifests are under Research/experiments/pulsechain_integrated_*_20261001.json. 
snapshot-headers.json records the correct boundary and endpoint. An earlier exploratory header request
used the wrong boundary and is expressly excluded. PulseChain historical state reads failed at the
selected public endpoint, so historical contract reads use Ethereum archive state at the matching
inherited header. This is an inherited-state reconstruction, not a later cross-chain equivalence
assumption.

How bridges, stablecoin issuers and pools can form one pDAI
support system
1 October 2026. Read-only research. This study extends the white paper (main paper). Protocol names
below identify candidate contract families; they do not identify the people controlling their keys.
The integrated mechanism
The strongest version of the proposal combines three sources of usable inventory: bridges that return
existing local tokens; issuers that create existing local tokens against accepted collateral or authorized
credit; and locally earned proceeds. A shared operator could move that inventory among Curve, Aave,
Balancer and ordinary liquidity pools. Supply controllers could replenish an expensive stablecoin or retire
an excess one. The operator would buy cheap eligible units, sell expensive units and preserve both sides
of its conversion promise.
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 240

Every arrow is a separate asset conversion or contract permission. L1 here means PulseChain; L2 means
the proposed pARB environment. Its present source deployments were not accessible in this research.
Ethereum and ordinary Arbitrum documentation establish upstream designs, not a running pARB
deployment.
The important improvement is that local reissuance is optional when a bridge already returns
the token the destination pool accepts. New collateral adapters matter when the output is a
different representation or when existing escrow cannot provide enough inventory.
The subsequent dedicated sUSD study (Appendix 66) adds its six inherited pool connections, mUSD
basket acceptance and copied Synthetix issuer-specific synth bridge. It illustrates why the final pool-
facing L1 address matters even when source addresses differ, and why issuer minting must be
distinguished from pARB escrow release. Its fresh destination observations retain their separate block
27,683,120 identity.
Which date and which pools?
“As at May 2023” is defined here as the inherited snapshot, 10 May 2023 at 22:36:11 UTC, Ethereum
block 17,232,999, hash 0xe5667f9cafb115b1dcfc36b0b569a5601f01dfa000698140a1298ef4f87e2e37. This is the
PulseChain inherited boundary, not the end of May. We verified that the Ethereum header matches the
inherited PulseChain header before reading historical Ethereum state.
Eight previously identified responsive Curve registry roots return 618 unique pools and 381 distinct
direct or underlying token identities at that boundary. Of those pools, 176 have exact 3CRV as a
direct coin and 64 have exact FRAXBP . T welve underlying-coin getters failed; the pools and their direct
coins remain in the catalogue. This pass did not measure historical pool balances. Registry membership
includes experimental, abandoned and possibly empty pools; it does not establish an active issuer or
available cash.
The later PulseChain registry census has 619 pools. Its extra pool is 
0x02ac4107893ba767177d69851dcd87bedc63ab22; its additional cWBTC identity is excluded from the inherited
catalogue. T wo historical listing reads beyond the historical count failed and were excluded. The
historical census cannot be relabelled as a live capacity measurement.
